business_scope.primary_industry_name: Manufacture of Portable Phased-Array Medical Diagnostic Scanners

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Luxembourg is a unitary civil law jurisdiction in the Napoleonic tradition, with modern commercial statutes and direct EU regulatory application)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (TFEU) — free movement of establishment, capital, and EU trade agreements
EU–Canada Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA), provisionally applied since 21 September 2017
EU–Japan Economic Partnership Agreement, in force since 1 February 2019
EU–Singapore Free Trade Agreement, in force since 21 November 2019
Luxembourg–China Double Taxation Agreement, as amended by protocol, in force
Luxembourg–United States Double Taxation Convention, in force
Benelux Economic Union framework treaties and the intra-Benelux double tax treaty network

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing (as amended, inter alia, by the Law of 17 July 2020 transposing Directive (EU) 2018/843); Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE), as amended; CSSF Regulation No. 12-02 of 14 December 2012, as amended; Law of 10 August 1915 concerning commercial companies (SARL provisions at Articles 180 et seq.).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing and certified extract of the commercial register of each corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent company registry of the shareholder's home jurisdiction, verified by the local notary or public officer
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille Certificate (1961 Hague Convention member states) or consular legalization by the Luxembourg embassy in the issuing state

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified passport copies of all ultimate beneficial owners, directors, and authorised signatories
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Home-state notary, consulate, or competent administrative authority
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille Certificate or consular legalization; certified French/German translation required where documents are not in an administrative language

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Original notarized power of attorney (procuration) executed by the constituting shareholder(s) in favour of the Luxembourg notary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary in the shareholder's jurisdiction; if executed in Luxembourg, a Luxembourg notary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille Certificate for foreign powers of attorney, or consular legalization where the issuing state is not party to the 1961 Hague Convention

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Draft articles of association (statuts) in French, to be executed as a notarial instrument (acte constitutif)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Domestic notarial authentication; no apostille required for the domestic RCS filing; certified notarial copies issued for foreign authorities

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended, Title V – Société à Responsabilité Limitée, Articles 710-1 et seq.; complemented by the Law of 19 December 2002 on the Luxembourg Business Registers and the Grand-Ducal Regulations on RCS electronic filing
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), Luxembourg
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarial deed of incorporation (acte de constitution) with annexed articles of association; registered with the RCS and published in RESA (Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: EUR 12,000 minimum subscribed and fully paid-up capital for a SARL under Article 710-1 et seq. of the Law of 10 August 1915. The funds must be deposited in a blocked bank account in Luxembourg, evidenced by a bank certificate delivered to the notary, and may be released to the company only upon successful RCS registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the company confirms and accepts the share subscriptions stated in the annexed articles, acknowledges receipt of the bank certificate evidencing full payment of subscribed capital, and records the shareholders in the company’s register. RESOLVED, that the registered office is fixed at 12, Rue de l’Innovation, L-5324 Contern, Luxembourg, and that all official correspondence shall be sent to this address. RESOLVED, that Ms. Camille Laurent is appointed sole manager with full powers of management and representation under the articles, and Mr. Jonas Weber is appointed authorized signatory for daily banking and operational matters. Both officers are empowered to open bank accounts, sign contracts, and complete incorporation follow-up formalities.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company name reservation and certificate of non-confusion
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File an online application through the Luxembourg Business Registers portal for a certificate of non-confusion (certificat de non-confusion) verifying that the proposed SARL name is distinguishable from existing registered entities and compliant with Luxembourg naming rules. Provide three alternative names in priority order. No notarial step is required at this stage.
required_dossiers: Online name reservation application
List of proposed company names in priority order
Copy of valid passport or national ID of the incorporator(s)
Signed power of attorney if submitted through a representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues a refusal on availability or conformity, file an amended application within five business days with corrected distinguishing elements. A second refusal may be appealed to the competent administrative court in accordance with the Luxembourg Business Registers law.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital deposit, blocked bank account and preparation of constitutive documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg notary and a Luxembourg credit institution or PCI (professionnel du secteur financier)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary blocked escrow account in the company's name with a Luxembourg bank and transfer the minimum share capital of EUR 12,000 via wire transfer. Upon confirmation of receipt, the bank issues a certificate attesting that the funds are deposited and blocked until RCS registration. Simultaneously instruct the notary with the approved name, draft articles of association, shareholder identities, manager details, and registered office address so that the notary can prepare the notarial deed.
required_dossiers: RCS certificate of non-confusion
Bank blocked-funds certificate evidencing EUR 12,000 paid-up capital
Draft articles of association
Identity documents of all shareholders and managers
Sworn declaration of good conduct and non-conviction of proposed managers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank queries the beneficial ownership structure, provide the request for additional information supported by the preliminary ownership chart and identity documents. If the bank refuses the escrow relationship, select an alternative Luxembourg bank or PCI and obtain a replacement blocked-funds certificate, then resubmit the notarization instructions.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the notarial deed of incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg notary public acting under the Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Attend execution of the notarial deed of incorporation (acte de constitution) before the Luxembourg notary. The notary reviews the statuts, verifies the blocked capital certificate, confirms the legality of the corporate purpose, confirms manager appointments, and reads the deed to the parties before signature. Immediately after execution, the notary transmits the signed notarial deed and standard filing form to the RCS for registration and publication.
required_dossiers: Drafted notarial deed of incorporation with annexed articles
Original bank blocked-funds certificate
RCS certificate of non-confusion
Identity documents of shareholders and managers
Proof of registered office address and landlord consent if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary detects a substantive defect, an acte rectificatif may be executed before the same notary to correct the deed. If RCS notifications delay registration, coordinate with the notary to resubmit the corrected filing within 15 days after the initial submission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The notary submits the signed notarial deed and the standard RCS filing form electronically to the RCS. The RCS verifies the file, assigns the company's registration number (R.C.S. Luxembourg number), and issues the certificate of registration. The deed is then published in the electronic official gazette RESA, which legally completes the company's formation and enforceability against third parties.
required_dossiers: Signed notarial deed of incorporation
RCS standard filing form
Beneficial owner identification declarations required by the Law of 13 January 2019
Proof of payment of RCS registration fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues an inquiry or query, respond through the LBR online dossier within one month; otherwise the application is rejected. After correction, resubmit the registration file and pay any outstanding fees. An RCS refusal is subject to action before the Tribunal d'arrondissement.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: VAT, social security, and business establishment authorization
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT); Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS); Ministère de l'Économie – Direction générale de l'industrie
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After RCS registration, file the Luxembourg VAT registration application with the AEDT and obtain a national VAT number. If the company will hire employees, register as an employer with the CCSS within eight days of the first hire. Apply for the mandatory business establishment authorization (autorisation d'établissement) for the manufacturing and commercial activity from the Ministry of the Economy, submitting the criminal record extract of the responsible manager and proof of professional capacity. Also register for the communal business tax with the competent commune.
required_dossiers: RCS registration certificate
Notarized articles of association
VAT registration form
Identity document and criminal record extract of the manager
Proof of professional capacity or relevant qualification for the manufacturing activity
Lease or ownership proof of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Ministry of the Economy refuses the business authorization, request administrative reconsideration within three months of notification. If the refusal is maintained, bring an appeal before the Tribunal administratif within the statutory time limit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Medical device manufacturer conformity and market access notification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Health – Direction de la Santé, Division de la Pharmacie et des Médicaments; EU notified body designated under Regulation (EU) 2017/745
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Before manufacturing portable phased-array medical diagnostic scanners and placing them on the EU market, establish a full quality management system compliant with ISO 13485 and Regulation (EU) 2017/745 (MDR). Appoint a person responsible for regulatory compliance (PRRC). Undergo conformity assessment by a notified body for the applicable device class, obtain CE marking, and file the EU Declaration of Conformity. Register as manufacturer and economic operator in EUDAMED and notify the Luxembourg Ministry of Health if the manufacturer's registered place of business is in Luxembourg. For export under Swift LC or TT payment rails, ensure all commercial invoices and declarations match the CE-marked technical file.
required_dossiers: ISO 13485 quality management system certificate
MDR technical documentation and clinical evaluation report
EU Declaration of Conformity and CE certificate issued by a notified body
EUDAMED manufacturer and device registration
PRRC appointment declaration
Post-market surveillance and vigilance procedure documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notified body issues nonconformities, submit a corrective action plan and verifiable evidence within the timeframe fixed by the notified body. If the Ministry of Health requests supplementary data, provide an amended technical file and obtain an updated notified body opinion before re-notification.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministère de l'Économie – Direction générale de l'industrie (General Directorate for Industry), Luxembourg
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorisation d'établissement (Business Establishment Authorization) for commercial and manufacturing activities under the amended Law of 28 December 1988 on access to the professions of artisan, trader, restaurateur, and service provider

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category C – registration/exemption for low-impact assembly and final manufacturing of electronic medical diagnostic devices; full Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) may be required if production scale, chemical solvent usage, or waste volumes exceed the thresholds defined by the Law of 15 May 2018 on environmental impact assessment and the Grand-Ducal regulations on classified establishments.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharges must meet the national implementation of Directive 2010/75/EU on industrial emissions: COD ≤125 mg/L, BOD5 ≤25 mg/L, suspended solids ≤35 mg/L, pH 6.5–9, and compliance with municipal sewer by-laws. Volatile organic compound (VOC) emissions must comply with the solvent emission limit values in the Grand-Ducal Regulation implementing Directive 2010/75/EU. Hazardous waste, including electronic components, soldering residues, and solvents, must be segregated, stored in approved containers, collected by an authorized waste management service, and recorded in the waste register.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate issued by the communal authority after inspection by the Service d'Incendie et de Secours (CGDIS) covering alarm systems, emergency exits, and extinguishing equipment; structural load clearance included in the commune's building permit with verification of the floor capacity for production and test equipment; occupational health and safety clearance from Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM) covering electrical safety, noise exposure, manual handling, machine guarding, and the medical surveillance of employees.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) – Luxembourg Inland Revenue (direct taxes); Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) – VAT Authority; Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) hosted by the Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS); Administration des douanes et accises (ADA) – Customs and Excise; unified e-government portal MyGuichet.lu operated by the State Information Technology Centre (CTIE) and requiring LuxTrust electronic authentication.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Notarize the SARL deed and file with the RCS via the Luxembourg Business Registers platform to obtain the commercial registration number and the 13-digit national identification number (matricule). Step 2: File the corporate income tax (IRC), municipal business tax (ICC), and net wealth tax (IFF) registration with ACD using the matricule; the ACD issues the direct tax file number. Step 3: Apply to AEDT for VAT registration on Form 640/641, obtaining the Luxembourg VAT identification number with the 'LU' prefix. Step 4: Apply to ADA for an EORI number to clear exports. Step 5: Foreign entities not established in Luxembourg that make taxable supplies of goods or services subject to VAT in Luxembourg must register directly with AEDT from the first taxable transaction, without any local turnover threshold; non-established suppliers may also use the One-Stop-Shop (OSS) for distance sales and electronically supplied services.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: A Luxembourg SARL is fully subject to entity-level taxation on worldwide profits, with no US-style check-the-box regime. Statutory elections include: (i) fiscal integration/group taxation (intégration fiscale) for qualifying groups with direct or indirect 95% ownership linking Luxembourg-resident companies and Luxembourg permanent establishments of EU/EEA companies; (ii) the participation exemption election for qualifying dividend income and capital gains on qualifying shareholdings (minimum 10% participation or EUR 1.2 million acquisition cost for dividends, and 10% participation held 12 months for capital gains, subject to anti-abuse and substance requirements); (iii) the small-enterprise VAT franchise option allowing exemption for turnover below EUR 35,000, with the elective right to apply normal VAT; (iv) reverse-charge self-assessment for intra-community acquisitions and imported services; and (v) mandatory hybrid mismatch adjustments under ATAD that override elective outcomes for cross-border hybrid entities.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT – Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée (TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general VAT registration threshold for established Luxembourg taxable persons; registration is compulsory from the first euro of taxable turnover. Small-business franchise exemption may apply below EUR 35,000 annual turnover excluding VAT, but the taxpayer can elect to waive the exemption. Non-established foreign suppliers have no registration threshold and must register from the first taxable transaction in Luxembourg, except where the customer is liable for VAT under the reverse-charge mechanism. Intra-EU distance sales of goods and certain digitally supplied services to non-taxable Luxembourg consumers trigger Luxembourg VAT registration only when the EUR 10,000 Union-wide annual threshold is exceeded, unless the supplier elects Luxembourg taxation through the OSS regime.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Luxembourg currently has no real-time fiscal clearance, no mandatory digital stamping, and no transactional API reporting obligation for B2B invoicing. E-invoicing is accepted provided that the invoice guarantees authenticity of origin, integrity of content, and legibility, typically through EDI, structured XML, or digital signature. A PEPPOL-based e-invoicing channel is available for B2G supplies, but not yet mandatory. Under the EU VAT in the Digital Age (ViDA) framework, Luxembourg is expected to adopt mandatory electronic invoicing and real-time digital transaction reporting from approximately 2030. AEDT requires retention of all VAT books and e-invoices for 10 years in a legible electronic format, and access must be available for the tax authority on demand.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: The 0% VAT rate applies to: (i) supplies of goods physically exported outside the European Union by the supplier or on its behalf, where prima facie proof of export is obtained within 90 days from the time of supply; (ii) intra-Community supplies of goods to a customer holding a valid VAT identification number in another EU Member State, with the supply reported in the VIES recapitulative statement; and (iii) certain offshore services, including installation, commissioning, calibration, and post-sale maintenance of the color Doppler ultrasound consoles performed outside the EU for a recipient established outside the EU, provided the services are directly linked to exported goods. The exporter must hold complete documentary evidence demonstrating that the goods left the EU customs territory and reached the foreign customer; the customs export declaration must be lodged electronically by the exporting SARL or its customs agent.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Electronic customs export declaration (SAD/EX-A) endorsed by Luxembourg Customs with a validated Movement Reference Number (MRN)
Commercial invoice and detailed packing list identifying the ultrasound console by model, serial number, quantity, and value
Bill of Lading (sea), CMR consignment note (road), or Air Waybill (air) evidencing physical carriage to a destination outside the EU
Transport contract and delivery note or proof of receipt signed by the foreign distributor/hospital evidencing arrival at the overseas destination
Bank inward remittance certificate or SWIFT MT103 credit advice demonstrating repatriation of the foreign-currency export proceeds to the Luxembourg SARL
VIES listing confirmation of the customer and recapitulative statement for intra-community supplies (where applicable)
Export licence, CE/medical-device clearance certificate, and importing-country regulatory approval, as required by the destination market
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Luxembourg AEDT applies strict scrutiny to export zero-rating claims, cross-checking the customs MRN, VIES records, transport documents, and bank receipts. A wrongly zero-rated export is reassessed at the standard 17% VAT, with statutory late-payment interest accruing monthly from the original due date, plus recovery of any input VAT improperly credited. In cases of fraudulent export claims, forged documentation, or artificial circular export arrangements, Luxembourg imposes administrative fines, retrospective clawback of all contested VAT refunds, and criminal penalties for tax fraud of up to EUR 250,000 and/or imprisonment for up to five years for the responsible directors. The limitation period for the tax administration to reassess and recover is prolonged to 10 years where fraud is established, with the burden of proving the physical export falling on the taxpayer.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL), a member of the Eurosystem. BCL performs monetary, payment-systems, and external-statistics functions. There is no separate foreign-exchange administration; the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) supervises banking conduct and AML/CFT compliance.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg provides full current-account and capital-account convertibility under Articles 63-65 TFEU. No exchange-control approval, licence, or repatriation permit is required to convert EUR or foreign currency, inject capital, pay suppliers, or remit dividends/profits abroad. The euro is fully convertible. Profit distribution from the SARL is constrained only by the solvency rules of the Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies (net-asset test and interim-accounts test for interim dividends) and by domestic dividend withholding tax, not by FX regulation.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Luxembourg and EU law impose no surrender obligation, mandatory conversion ratio, or holding-period restriction on export proceeds. The SARL may retain 100% of EUR and foreign-currency export receipts onshore or offshore, subject only to BCL balance-of-payments/external-statistics declarations when triggering reporting thresholds.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE – Spuerkeess)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium for operational treasury only. EU-authorised fintech/EMI providers (e.g., Airwallex, Revolut Business, MultiPass) may passport into Luxembourg under PSD2, but they cannot hold the capital-escrow account, cannot issue documentary commercial letters of credit, and often rely on third-party correspondent banks for high-value MT103 flows required for medical-device trade. They are adequate for sub-€50,000 collection/disbursement flows and payroll; the principal clearing account and all USD/CNH trade settlements should remain with a Tier-1 domestic bank. Legal constraints: a non-EEA EMI must hold an EEA/Luxembourg authorisation to provide services locally, and all transfers must satisfy the Transfer of Funds Regulation (EU) 2015/847 with complete originator and beneficiary data.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: There is no statutory requirement for physical appearance; CSSF-compliant video-identification is accepted in principle. In practice, Tier-1 banks require either a physical meeting with the gérant and each UBO or a video-KYC session through an approved remote-identification provider, plus an apostilled/notarised corporate pack. For a non-resident-owned SARL with limited local substance, one physical visit to Luxembourg for the signing meeting and bank interview is strongly advised to avoid a 6-10 week onboarding delay. The share capital must be blocked on a Luxembourg account before registration.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident UBOs in a FATF grey-list or high-corruption-risk jurisdiction, or a nominee/opaque ownership structure.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: FATF/EU list screening; independent background and source-of-wealth report; tax residence certificates; notarised corporate chart and UBO register under the Law of 13 January 2019; substance evidence in Luxembourg (lease, business plan, draft employment contracts); CRS/FATCA self-certifications.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High unit values and trade turnover for Color Doppler Ultrasound Consoles (ISIC 3250) with third-country distributors, creating invoice-price verification risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed distributor agreements; pro-forma and commercial invoices; bills of lading/airway bills; customs declarations; independent benchmark study for the device; transfer-pricing file under the OECD Transfer Pricing Guidelines for any related-party margin.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payment mismatches: funds received from an entity different from the named buyer, or rapid T+0/T+1 onward transmission of nearly all received funds.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Unbroken chain of contracts and sales agreements; treasury policy and reconciliation ledger; legal opinion confirming the flow is not a pass-through; Transfer of Funds Regulation data for every leg; written declarations of the beneficial owner of each incoming payment.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Early profit distribution or shareholder-advance repayment within 3-6 months after a capital injection, indicating possible conduit or round-tripping abuse.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Solvency test calculation under the Law of 10 August 1915; interim or first annual accounts; legal opinion of a Luxembourg avocat; advance tax ruling if obtained; shareholder minutes and dividend distribution report.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Dual-use or cryptographic components embedded in the ultrasound console, or incomplete end-user documentation for exports to high-risk regions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: ECCN/HS classification memo; EU Dual-Use Regulation 2021/821 licence or EU001 General Export Authorisation assessment; signed end-user certificates; customs classification rulings; supplier compliance declarations; sanctions-screening output.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital injection from the non-resident shareholder to the SARL: single SWIFT MT103 in EUR with an unbroken reference chain — shareholder's name, the company's RCS/LEI, the notarial deed or board resolution, and the BCL external-statistics purpose code for 'direct investment – equity capital'. For EEA-based shareholders, a SEPA Credit Transfer may be used only below the bank's reporting threshold; otherwise MT103 is mandatory. Funds must be credited and blocked on the capital escrow account at a Luxembourg credit institution before the notary obtains the 'blocage de fonds' certificate and RCS registration is completed. Applicable SARL capital requirement: minimum €12,000, at least half (€6,000) paid in cash at incorporation. Do not split payments or mix trade invoices with equity transfers.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: (1) Open-account or advance-payment settlements to suppliers of components, display systems, and transducers: SWIFT MT103 with commercial-invoice reference and full Transfer of Funds Regulation data — TARGET2 for EUR, correspondent clearing via CHIPS/Fedwire for USD. (2) Documentary trade: issue of a commercial letter of credit through the Luxembourg bank's trade desk (SWIFT MT700), governed by ICC UCP 600, with the beneficiary's confirming/negotiating bank outside Luxembourg. (3) EU supplier payments below €500,000 can be executed via SEPA Credit Transfer and SEPA Instant. (4) Liquidity policy: maintain a target balance equal to 3-5 weeks of operating costs and keep USD/CNH sweep lines active; centralise all FX and LC operations at the primary operating account with BGL BNP Paribas.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright deliverable FX forward on EUR/USD, EUR/CNH, and EUR/JPY with tenor up to 12 months, executed under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement with a Luxembourg/EU-licensed credit institution, subject to EMIR trade reporting.
FX swap (principal and interest swapped between two currencies) for short-term liquidity and working-capital management.
Cross-currency interest-rate swap (XCCY) for medium-term equipment financing or LC reimbursement facilities denominated in USD.
European-style plain vanilla FX option (EUR call/USD put or EUR put/USD call) purchased from a licensed bank, with premium risk capped to an approved budget.
Non-deliverable forward (NDF) for currencies without deliverable markets (e.g., CNY, INR, BRL), settled in USD/EUR, provided the counterparty bank maintains an NDF booking desk.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual general meeting and adoption of annual accounts
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders' general meeting (internal formality; minutes retained in statutory records)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the financial year-end; for a 31 December year-end, no later than 30 June
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors and managers are civilly liable for failure to convene the meeting; persistent failure may lead to court-ordered compliance and, ultimately, judicial dissolution or strike-off proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Deposit of annual financial statements with the commercial and companies register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) / Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 1 month after shareholder approval and in all cases within 7 months of the financial year-end; for a 31 December year-end, by 31 July
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalties and director liability; two consecutive years of non-filing may trigger enforcement by the RCS and administrative strike-off (radiation) with possible judicial dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax and net wealth tax return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD), Luxembourg tax administration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a 31 December year-end, due by 31 May of the following year; an extension to 31 December may be granted by the tax administration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default assessment, monthly statutory late-payment interest, and late-filing fines up to EUR 2,500; continued non-filing exposes the company to enforced tax collection and loss of administrative clearances.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% (Luxembourg City): 15.00% CIT + 1.05% solidarity surcharge (7% on CIT for profits above EUR 25,000) + 6.75% municipal business tax (commune of Luxembourg), after standard deductibility alignment.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: IP income box: 80% exemption on net qualifying IP income (patents, certified software; effective rate approx. 4.99%–5.17%). Participation exemption: 100% CIT and net wealth tax exemption on qualifying dividends and capital gains (>=10% holding or EUR 1.2M cost, >=12 months). Notional Interest Deduction on qualifying new equity contributions. No Luxembourg WHT on outbound interest/royalties (0%) in ordinary cases.
